claim: autoSaveId persists panel sizes to localStorage; optional storage prop swaps the backing store (e.g. cookie) to avoid SSR flicker.
quote: Panel groups with an autoSaveId prop will automatically save and restore their layouts on mount. By default this library uses localStorage... an optional storage prop... makes it easier to persist layouts somewhere other than localStorage (e.g. like a Cookie).

claim: PanelGroupStorage is a synchronous getItem/setItem interface; onLayout fires on layout change; conditionally-rendered Panels need stable id and order props.
quote: getItem: (name:string) => string; setItem: (name: string, value: string) => void ... onLayout | ?(sizes: number[]) => void ... When panels are conditionally rendered though, it's best to supply these values (id and order).

claim: Dockview serializes with api.toJSON() returning SerializedDockview; onDidLayoutChange lets you autosave on every change.
quote: toJSON(): SerializedDockview ... onDidLayoutChange: Event<void> ... You can set up an automatic save mechanism that captures the layout whenever it changes and stores it to local storage or a database.

claim: fromJSON deserializes a layout; an invalid or corrupted layout throws and the dock resets gracefully; reuseExistingPanels option exists.
quote: fromJSON(data: SerializedDockview, options: { reuseExistingPanels: boolean }): void ... If you try to load an invalid or corrupted layout the dock will throw an Error and the dock will reset gracefully ready for another attempt with a valid object.

claim: A saved layout referencing a component name that no longer exists throws in fromJSON and could wedge the dock; maintainer calls invalid component names the most likely form of layout corruption.
quote: Invalid component names are probably the single most likely form of layout corruption so I think this is an important case to handle cleanly.

claim: Modern docking libraries (Dockview, FlexLayout, Gridstack) all offer built-in toJSON/fromJSON serialization to persist and restore window arrangements per user.
quote: All major alternatives like Dockview, FlexLayout, and Gridstack.js offer built-in API serialization methods like toJSON() and fromJSON()... restore the exact window arrangements whenever the user logs back in.

claim: rc-dock exposes saveLayout()/loadLayout(); tabs are stored by ID and content is rehydrated through the loadTab callback.
FlexLayout model JSON is {global, layout(row/tabset/tab), borders, subLayouts}; Model.fromJson/toJson serialize it; a factory resolves each tab's component name to a React element.
quote: const model = Model.fromJson(jsonObject); const json = model.toJson(); ... const factory = (node) => { const component = node.getComponent(); ... }

claim: Allotment onChange fires with an array of numbers on drag (debounce recommended); defaultSizes and the imperative resize() ref method restore sizes.
quote: Callback that is fired when the pane sizes change (usually on drag). Recommended to add a debounce function... Passed an array of numbers. ... call its reset and resize methods manually.

claim: SerializedDockview contains a grid (root branch/leaf tree with width/height/orientation), a panels map (id, contentComponent, title) and an activeGroup identifier.
quote: grid: root structure with branch/leaf types... panels: object containing panel definitions with id, contentComponent, and title... activeGroup: identifier for the currently active group.

claim: Dockview panels are registered by name through the components dock option, and restoration resolves saved names against that registry.
quote: You can register panels through the dock option components.

claim: react-resizable-panels stores sizes under key react-resizable-panels:<autoSaveId>; changing panel count makes the entry stale, fixed by bumping autoSaveId or clearing the key; cookie+defaultSize gives flash-free SSR.
quote: The library serializes sizes to localStorage under react-resizable-panels:<autoSaveId> ... When you change layout shape (number of panels), localStorage entries become stale. Either bump autoSaveId or read/clear the old key.
